notes.title: Justified by faith “apart from works of the law”
notes.intro: Paul says a person is justified by faith apart from works of the law. This verse was at the heart of the Reformation.

views.label: By faith alone
views.summary: Lutheran and Reformed Christians read Paul as teaching that people are declared righteous by faith alone, not by any works; good works follow as fruit.
views.source: Augsburg Confession, Article IV; Westminster Confession 11

views.label: Not by works of the Mosaic law, but by grace that transforms
views.summary: Catholic teaching agrees that justification cannot be earned, but understands it as including inner renewal through faith and baptism, with grace bearing fruit in love.

views.label: Part of a lifelong process of union with God
views.summary: Orthodox Christians tend to read Paul’s words within the larger picture of salvation as healing and union with God (theosis).
views.source: Fr Thomas Hopko, The Orthodox Faith, vol. 4

notes.common: In 1999 the Lutheran World Federation and the Catholic Church signed a Joint Declaration on the Doctrine of Justification, finding a “consensus in basic truths.”
